drafts.title: Deliver consistently strong, linear power delivery while retaining sporty, planted feel
drafts.description: When you accelerate or change drive modes the car feels powerful, smooth and predictable — no jerks, surges, or delayed response — while keeping the current sporty, planted driving character.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a pre-launch real-world validation (n=200 drivers; 1,000+ throttle events across city/highway/launch conditions) ≤2% of throttle events produce perceivable jerks, delayed responses or abrupt surges as reported by drivers and measured by torque/response telemetry.
assumptions: Engine/e-motor control and calibration updates are feasible within a successor lifecycle without major hardware redesign
Sufficient telemetry can be captured in validation to detect perceptible torque anomalies
uncertainties: Some rare customer-reported powertrain behaviors may originate from third-party software or service conditions not reproducible in tests

drafts.title: Keep and validate the car’s smooth, comfortable ride together with responsive handling
drafts.description: Passengers experience a quiet, cushioned ride on daily drives and long trips while drivers still feel a sporty, responsive chassis that stays planted and confident.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a standardized 50‑mile mixed-route study, at least 85% of participants rate ride comfort in the top‑2 categories (satisfied/top‑2) compared with the current model baseline; lateral handling responsiveness metrics meet or exceed current model targets during the same test route.
assumptions: Chassis tuning and available suspension hardware for the successor can match current model’s comfort/handling balance
Standardized participant study of sufficient size (n≥100) will be run for validation
uncertainties: Optional suspension packages (air vs steel) may shift subjective comfort scores between customer segments
drafts.scope_reason: Preserve and validate core driving experience

drafts.title: Seats that fit more body sizes: greater height range, adjustable firmness and clear controls
drafts.description: Short and tall drivers can quickly find a safe, comfortable seating position with enough height to see over the hood; seat comfort settings adapt to body size and memory stores for drivers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Seat cushion height provides at least 100 mm (10 cm) of adjustable range from lowest to highest position; at least three preset firmness profiles are available and 95% of test users (n=100 across a height range) can achieve a clear forward view over the hood and a comfortable posture in ≤60 seconds.
assumptions: Seat actuator packaging on the successor permits a larger vertical travel range without reducing occupant safety
User study with broad height distribution will be conducted to validate visibility
uncertainties: Increasing vertical travel may require compromises with seat cushion length or mounting that must be validated for safety and durability
drafts.scope_reason: Direct customer outcome about seat experience

drafts.title: Reliable hands‑free trunk and predictable Comfort Access behavior
drafts.description: When your hands are full the touchless kick‑to‑open trunk opens reliably on the first try, never opens randomly, and Comfort Access unlock behavior is consistent and discoverable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands‑free trunk opens on the first correct gesture within 1.0 second in ≥95% of 100 varied real‑world tests (different shoes, footwear, luggage) and there are zero instances of unintended trunk opens in a 1,000‑hour parked state test; Comfort Access can be set to ‘unlock all doors’ in a visible menu path within two taps and executes for ≥95% of authorized proximity events.
assumptions: Sensor and software improvements can reduce false negatives/positives without adding intrusive new hardware
Validation will include real‑world scenarios (wet shoes, key in bag, crowded parking)
uncertainties: Environmental conditions (snow, mud) may still increase false negatives and will need separate tuning
drafts.scope_reason: Customer‑visible behavior of trunk and access

drafts.title: Proximity unlock opens all vehicle doors reliably and the behavior is easy to change
drafts.description: Approaching the car with an authorized key opens all doors (not just driver door) unless the user explicitly selects a different behavior; the setting is easy to find and change.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Proximity unlock opens all doors in ≥95% of authorized approach events in mixed parking scenarios; the setting to change unlock behavior is discoverable within two taps from the vehicle’s main settings screen and confirmed by user testing (≥90% success).
assumptions: Comfort Access firmware and UI can expose the setting without added hardware
Validation will include different approach angles and keyfob/bag placements
uncertainties: Aftermarket keyfobs or third‑party keys may behave differently and affect some edge cases

drafts.title: Allow drivers to permanently disable automatic engine stop‑start if they prefer
drafts.description: Drivers who find auto stop‑start annoying can set the system to remain off by default and the car honors that setting every time.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle provides a user‑settable default for engine stop‑start set to ‘off’ that persists across ignition cycles and is honored 100% of the time in validation tests.
assumptions: Regulatory conditions allow a user choice for stop‑start behavior
Software persistence across power cycles is implementable without hardware changes
uncertainties: In rare cases, emissions-driven mandates or warranty requirements could limit full persistence in some markets

drafts.title: Keep the large, premium touchscreen look while making core controls discoverable and less distracting
drafts.description: The long dash display remains a visual strength but core functions (temperature, vent direction, fan speed, odometer/trip, media controls) are reachable quickly and do not require deep menu navigation or distracting eyes‑off time; the screen resists smudging and remains readable in bright light.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Core controls (climate temp, vent direction, fan speed, odometer/trip, play/pause) are reachable in ≤3 touches and climate/vent adjustments can be completed within 2 seconds by users during driving tests; 90% success rate in a 200‑person usability study; screen surface shows a ≥30% reduction in visible smudging under standard finger oil tests and meets a daytime legibility threshold in >80,000 lux glare test defined by UX lab.
assumptions: Usability improvements can combine a small set of physical or haptic controls/shortcuts with software changes
Anti‑smudge and anti‑glare coatings with the stated performance are available for production
uncertainties: Some customers will still prefer more physical knobs; satisfaction will vary by user preference
drafts.scope_reason: Directly addresses multiple infotainment and HVAC discoverability complaints while keeping a praised design element

drafts.title: Smartphone integration, voice and in‑car connectivity must be reliable and fast
drafts.description: Phone mirroring (Apple CarPlay), voice commands, wireless charging and in‑car Wi‑Fi work reliably without repeated disconnections and the wireless charger fits and charges major phone models under typical conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Apple CarPlay connects and maintains a stable session in ≥98% of 1,000 connection attempts across current iPhone models; voice commands correctly understand and execute named tasks in ≥90% of controlled phrase tests; wireless charger delivers ≥7.5W to 95% of tested phone models with common cases and holds the phone during 0.3 g lateral acceleration; in‑car Wi‑Fi connects and sustains a benchmark throughput (e.g., streaming 5 Mbps) in ≥95% of tests.
assumptions: Validation will use a representative set of phone makes/models and case types available at launch
Cellular/Wi‑Fi performance depends partly on external networks and will be measured under controlled network conditions
uncertainties: Third‑party phone OS updates can change compatibility after launch and may require software updates

drafts.title: Displayed electric range must be accurate and stable across conditions
drafts.description: The range shown to the driver reflects real-world expectations, minimizing anxiety on longer drives and giving trustworthy guidance for planning charging.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across validation drives in cold, moderate and hot climates (aggregated n≥2,000 miles of logged trips), the displayed electric range has a mean error ≤7% and standard deviation ≤5% compared with measured remaining range to empty.
assumptions: Improved state‑of‑charge and range estimation algorithms with telematics exposure to fleet data are available for the successor
Validation includes typical cabin loads (HVAC, payload) and temperatures
uncertainties: Extreme driving styles and conditions (very cold climates, sustained high speeds) will still produce larger deviations
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-facing requirement about range display accuracy

drafts.title: Faster and more predictable charging with clear station compatibility guidance
drafts.description: Charging sessions reach useful energy levels quickly when a fast charger is available and the car helps drivers find compatible and available charging stations.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At DC fast chargers supporting ≥150 kW, the vehicle reaches 80% state of charge within ≤30 minutes when battery preconditioning is active (measured in controlled tests); scheduled AC charging begins within ±5 minutes of the scheduled time in ≥98% of trials; in‑car charging guidance identifies compatible and verified stations and displays occupancy/availability info for ≥80% of queried areas in the U.S. beta geography.
assumptions: Vehicle battery chemistry and thermal management support peak acceptance near 150 kW under normal SOC windows
Network partnerships or verified third‑party data provide station compatibility and occupancy info
uncertainties: Third‑party charger reliability and local infrastructure availability remain outside BMW’s direct control
drafts.scope_reason: Customer outcomes for charging speed and navigation to chargers

drafts.title: Braking that is quiet, non‑grabby and produces acceptable brake dust
drafts.description: Braking feels smooth and predictable without loud squeal or a grabby sensation; brake dust is controlled so wheel appearance and cleanup are reasonable for premium buyers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In laboratory NVH tests and a 200‑vehicle fleet durability program (first 6 months), persistent squeal or grinding occurs in ≤1% of vehicles; subjective braking comfort scores reach the top‑2 (satisfied) in ≥85% of drivers; measured brake dust covers ≤15% of the visible wheel face after the first 1,000 miles under standardized test cycles.
assumptions: Brake pad compound and rotor design changes can materially reduce squeal and dust without compromising stopping performance
Fleet validation program will expose early-life phenomena
uncertainties: Tire/wheel finish and regional brake material suppliers can influence dust appearance and may vary by market
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-visible brake NVH and dust behavior

drafts.title: Sufficient, well‑placed interior storage and clear owner‑usable compartments
drafts.description: Owners can store everyday items (large water bottle, phone, small bag) in dedicated, easy‑reach places without shuffling items, and storage areas include cord routing and secure lidded spaces.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 300‑participant study, ≥85% of users rate interior storage as sufficient (top‑2) and can stow one 1‑liter bottle plus a medium bag in reachable storage without removing other items; glovebox/center console provide a covered, lockable compartment and at least one routed charging path.
assumptions: Packaging tradeoffs allow modest increases or re‑arrangement of storage without major architecture changes
uncertainties: Some accessory items vary by market and affect perceived sufficiency

drafts.title: Make My Modes more discoverable and persistent while keeping their customization value
drafts.description: Drivers can easily create, name and activate personalized My Modes (drive, lighting, HUD, seats) and rely on them to persist and be quickly selectable for specific trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Users can create and activate a My Mode with at least three saved settings in ≤4 taps from the home screen and modes persist across ignition cycles; 90% success rate in a 150‑user usability test.
assumptions: UI changes can be implemented without affecting core vehicle controls
Mode persistence storage is available in vehicle user profile architecture
uncertainties: Some users may prefer fewer defaults; discoverability improvements must balance not overcomplicating the home screen
drafts.scope_reason: Improves a praised feature and addresses discoverability complaints

drafts.title: Broaden interior and exterior personalization: more palettes, ambient lighting scenes and optional panoramic roof
drafts.description: Customers can choose richer interior and exterior styling and mood lighting to match tastes, including an optional panoramic glass roof with adjustable shading.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At launch offer at least 5 interior design palettes, 12 ambient lighting scenes and an optional panoramic glass roof with user‑operable shade; in a 300‑person preference study ≥80% rate available options as satisfactory.
assumptions: Material sourcing and roof packaging are feasible for an optional package
Preference studies will guide palette and lighting choices
uncertainties: Some exterior design changes may split opinions; optional packages help mitigate this risk

drafts.title: Keep the highway assistant reliability and expand long‑commute usability
drafts.description: Highway driving and long commutes feel easier because the highway assistant maintains lane and speed reliably and integrates naturally into driver workflows.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On approved highways and supported routes the highway assistant maintains lane centering and speed control with lane deviation ≤0.3 m and speed tracking within ±3 mph for 95% of a 1,000‑mile fleet test; long‑commute satisfaction (top‑2) is ≥90% in a dedicated commuter study.
assumptions: Highway assistant sensors and maps remain accurate across targeted U.S. corridors
Validation includes varied traffic and weather conditions
uncertainties: Regulatory or map coverage changes could affect available functionality in specific regions
drafts.scope_reason: Preserve a voiced strength and validate it

drafts.title: Bet: Build a software‑defined cockpit with advanced HMI and wellness personalization
drafts.description: Customers experience a cockpit that adapts to them — driver profiles automatically change climate, seat, lighting and display content; the cabin monitors and improves air quality and offers wellness features that feel premium and useful.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At launch the vehicle supports per‑driver profiles that automatically apply seat, climate, lighting and display presets and completes profile activation tasks correctly in ≥90% of user trials (n=200); cabin air quality sensors and recirculation controls reduce PM2.5 by ≥30% within 10 minutes in a standardized test case.
assumptions: By the successor timeframe (3–5 years) sensors, compute and software architecture costs for advanced HMI and basic biometric/wellness sensors decline to permit integration in the 5‑Series
Customers value and will use personalized profiles tied to biometric or smartphone identity
uncertainties: Regulatory and privacy rules for biometric data vary by market and may limit which wellness features can be deployed
User acceptance of persistent biometric monitoring is uncertain
drafts.scope_reason: Forward-looking customer outcome deriving from trend in premium cockpits

drafts.title: Bet: Prepare for conditional (SAE Level‑3) highway automation when regulations and cost allow
drafts.description: When regulations permit and supplier costs fall, customers can use a certified conditional hands‑free mode on qualifying highways that handles sustained driving and requests takeovers in a clear, timely way.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System design supports sustained hands‑free operation on mapped highways for at least 30 minutes of continuous driving in test scenarios; when enabled and certified the system issues clear takeover requests with an auditable 5‑second minimum lead time and maintains safe state handling for ≥95% of defined highway scenarios in validation.
assumptions: Regulatory approval for conditional automation is available in target U.S. jurisdictions by launch or via staged deployment
LiDAR or equivalent sensor cost and supplier availability reach price/performance targets that make Level‑3 commercially viable for a mid‑luxury sedan
uncertainties: Regulatory and supplier constraints observed in the trend may delay or limit rollout — this is a conditional bet dependent on external factors
drafts.scope_reason: Strategic bet tied to industry trend for future driver assistance capabilities
